newsitem.title: USA: Original accuser will testify in Army sex case.
newsitem.headline: Original accuser will testify in Army sex case.

text.p: An alleged victim who has refused to testify in the sexual harassment and sexual assault case against the Army's top enlisted man must tell her story under oath, an Army hearing officer said on Thursday.
Retired Sgt. Maj. Brenda Hoster will testify, either voluntarily in a deposition or by force in a hearing should the Army recall her to active duty, Army officials have decided.

Hoster is the key witness against Gene McKinney, a 29-year Army veteran who became the first black American to hold the title of Sergeant Major of the Army, the chief advocate for the Army's enlisted soldiers.
Army officials were unable to confirm broadcast media reports late on Thursday that Hoster had agreed to testify after receiving assurances that she would not be questioned about her sexual past.
Hoster's attorney Susan Barnes did not immediately return calls to her Denver office.

Hoster's lawyers have said she is reluctant to testify for fears defence lawyers will pry into her sexual past. Another soldier has given a sworn statement that she witnessed Hoster having sex with another woman in Army barracks, which would be a violation of military law.

Her testimony is important because she was the original accuser against McKinney. After she took her story public, three other service women came forward, alleging that McKinney relentlessly pursued them for sex, using his powerful post to threaten their careers if they refused.
McKinney, 46, vehemently denies all the charges against him. He faces 18 counts including indecent assault, adultery and obstruction of justice.

Col. Robert Jarvis, the officer acting as a judge in a preliminary hearing to determine whether McKinney will be court-martialed, told the hearing on Thursday that his superiors have agreed to summon Hoster to a deposition.
A deposition is a sworn statement subject to cross examination that is taken outside the courtroom, usually in a law office.
